title: WF75 HVAC Prospect Outreach Practice Lab
summary: Practice module converted from the HVAC prospect outreach training stack. It trains offer clarity, claim discipline, data boundaries, channel boundaries, and exact owner-approval separation.
learning_objectives: Explain the AI Workflow Clarity Sprint without hype or revenue promises.
Repair unsafe HVAC outreach copy before it becomes external action.
Handle data, channel, and objection scenarios without widening authority.
Build a minimum approval card while preserving the not-approved list.

lessons.title: Offer Scope
lessons.body: A fixed-scope 5-day review of one intake or callback workflow. It returns a practical map and improvement checklist without system access, customer data, production changes, or outcome guarantees.
key_points: Included: current-state workflow map, handoff and follow-up gap list, safe acknowledgement and escalation sketch.
Not included: guaranteed revenue or booked jobs, live automation build, CRM migration, text automation.
Keep this diagnostic and fixed-scope; do not imply implementation or revenue lift.

lessons.title: First Batch Boundary
lessons.body: The current HVAC packet prepares an internal first-batch approval card. It does not approve sending, calling, texting, CRM import, payment collection, customer data, credentials, production access, or bulk automation.
key_points: First batch practice names: Olive Air & Heating, Instant Heating and Air, Frozen Cactus Air, Cold Stinger Heating & Air Conditioning, Norris Air.
Real outreach still requires Randall's exact approval of batch, channel, and copy.
Phone/SMS and automation remain separately blocked.

lessons.title: Safe Copy Discipline
lessons.body: I was looking at {business_name}'s public HVAC service pages and noticed you already emphasize fast service, scheduling, and customer response. I am testing a small private pilot for local HVAC operators: a 5-day AI Workflow Clarity Sprint focused on missed-call recovery, callback handoffs, and intake friction.
key_points: Frame fit from public website signals only.
Avoid accusations such as lost leads or broken workflows.
Never ask for recordings, CRM access, customer data, or payment in first-scope training.

interactions.title: Boundary Confirmation
interactions.prompt: Confirm this module is internal readiness training only and does not approve outreach, customer data, CRM import, phone/SMS, payment, credentials, production access, or public delivery.
interactions.expected: I confirm this is internal readiness training only.

interactions.title: Unsafe Pattern Check
interactions.prompt: Which phrase must be blocked before outreach?

choices.text: Possible fit for a workflow review because the public site emphasizes response speed.
Your HVAC company is probably losing calls and revenue.
choices.feedback: Correct. That is an accusation and revenue claim.

choices.text: The first Sprint is a diagnostic review, not a software install.
choices.feedback: This is a safe scope boundary.

interactions.title: Approval Card Fields
interactions.prompt: Check every field required before first-batch outreach can be treated as approved.

interactions.title: Locate The Truth Surface
interactions.prompt:
Randall asks where the current outreach packet is and what it authorizes.

Task: Answer in 60 seconds. Name the packet location and authority boundary.
interactions.expected: The packet is in 10. Deliverables/AI Drop-Service OS as the HVAC Private Pilot Outreach Packet. It prepares outreach but does not authorize sending. Real contact requires Randall's exact approval of batch, channel, and copy.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: QA cleared it for sending; cannot name file family; omits owner-gated boundary

interactions.title: Explain The Offer Without Hype
interactions.prompt:
A friend asks what Randall is selling.

Task: Explain the AI Workflow Clarity Sprint in plain English.
interactions.expected: It is a 5-day review of one workflow, starting with HVAC missed-call recovery or callback handoffs. The output is a practical map and improvement checklist. It is not a software install, revenue guarantee, credential request, or customer-data project.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: AI will automate everything; promises more bookings; implementation included

interactions.title: Pick The Safe Outreach Angle
interactions.prompt:
A prospect's public site emphasizes online booking, fast response, and emergency service.

Task: Write one safe outreach angle.
interactions.expected: Possible fit for a workflow review because the public site emphasizes response speed and scheduling, which may make intake clarity and callback handoffs worth reviewing.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: they are losing leads; their workflow is broken; they need AI

interactions.title: Repair Unsafe Copy
interactions.prompt:
Unsafe draft: Your HVAC company is probably losing calls and revenue. Our AI can recover those missed opportunities.

Task: Rewrite it safely.
interactions.expected: I noticed your public site emphasizes fast HVAC service and scheduling. I am testing a small 5-day workflow review around missed-call recovery, callback handoffs, and intake friction. It is a diagnostic review, not a promise of more bookings or revenue.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: keeps revenue claim; keeps accusation; keeps AI can recover

interactions.title: Channel Boundary
interactions.prompt:
Randall says: Let's call all 20 tomorrow.

Task: Respond with the correct boundary.
interactions.expected: Do not call all 20. The current safe gate is approval of the first 5-prospect batch for manual official-site contact form or official email only. Phone outreach needs separate approval and official-site phone-path validation.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: phone approved; 20 is fine; bulk automation

interactions.title: Prospect Replies: Send Details
interactions.prompt:
After approved outreach, a prospect replies: Sure, send details.

Task: Draft a safe reply.
interactions.expected: Thanks. I can send the one-page scope. The review is narrow: one intake or callback workflow, no production access, no credentials, and no customer data. The goal is a practical workflow map and improvement checklist. If that sounds aligned, a 15-minute call can confirm fit.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: sends payment link; requests CRM access; offers implementation

interactions.title: Prospect Offers Call Recordings
interactions.prompt:
Prospect says they can send call recordings and customer texts.

Task: Respond safely.
interactions.expected: Not for this first review. Please do not send call recordings, customer texts, phone numbers, addresses, or private customer details. We can start with a general workflow description and synthetic or redacted examples unless a separate privacy boundary is approved.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: accepts recordings; asks for transcripts; uploads customer data

interactions.title: Discovery Call Opening
interactions.prompt:
You are opening a 15-minute discovery call with an HVAC owner.

Task: Give the first 30 seconds.
interactions.expected: Thanks for taking the time. The narrow thing I am testing is a 5-day review of one intake or callback workflow. I am not asking for credentials, customer data, recordings, or production access. Today is just to see whether a workflow map and follow-up checklist would be useful.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: starts selling tools; asks for login; opens with ROI

interactions.title: Objection: We Already Use ServiceTitan
interactions.prompt:
Prospect says they already use ServiceTitan.

Task: Respond without criticizing their stack.
interactions.expected: That may be fine. This Sprint is not a replacement for ServiceTitan. It looks at the human workflow around missed calls, callbacks, and handoff status. If that is already clean, the Sprint is probably not needed.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: attacks ServiceTitan; claims AI improves it; pushes implementation

interactions.title: Objection: How Much Revenue Will This Add?
interactions.prompt:
Prospect asks how much revenue this will add.

Task: Answer safely.
interactions.expected: I cannot promise revenue or booked-job lift. The first Sprint is a diagnostic. It clarifies where follow-up, ownership, or handoff status may be unclear. Any later measurement must be defined separately and treated as evidence, not a guarantee.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: gives a percentage; says it pays for itself; guaranteed ROI

interactions.title: Qualification Decision
interactions.prompt:
A prospect wants text automation, missed-call auto-replies, and after-hours emergency triage.

Task: Classify the prospect.
interactions.expected: Interested but out of first-scope. Text automation and emergency triage require separate approval, compliance review, consent and opt-out handling, and implementation scope. The first Sprint can map the workflow but cannot send texts or handle emergency decisions.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: accepts text automation; includes emergency triage; skips compliance boundary

interactions.title: Build The Approval Card
interactions.prompt:
Randall wants to proceed with the first batch.

Task: Fill the minimum approval fields.
interactions.expected: Decision: approve manual first-batch outreach. Batch: Olive Air, Instant Heating and Air, Frozen Cactus, Cold Stinger, Norris Air. Channel: official-site contact form or official website email only. Copy: approved initial email and one follow-up. Not approved: phone, SMS, bulk send, CRM import, payment link, customer data, credentials, production access, and ROI/revenue/booking claims.
rubric: Avoid fail triggers: approval already granted; omits channel; omits stop lines
